# Lab 23.3: Managed Disaster Recovery

## What We Are Going to Do
Create an Enterprise Plus failover reservation with a secondary region and attach a replicated dataset to it, so both compute and data can fail over together. Enterprise Plus slots are billed every hour, so finish Labs 23.3–23.4 together.

## Steps

1. **[Console] Create the failover reservation.** **Workload management → Create reservation**:
   - **Name**: `lab-dr`, **Location**: `us-central1`
   - **Edition**: Enterprise Plus, **Baseline**: 50 slots
   - **Secondary location**: `us-east4`

   The CLI version:


<div style="margin:18px 0;border:1px solid #334155;border-radius:8px;overflow:hidden;">
<div style="background:#243244;color:#DBEAFE;padding:7px 12px;font-family:Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif;font-size:12px;font-weight:700;">
CODE • BASH
</div>
<pre style="margin:0;background:#111827;color:#F3F4F6;padding:16px;overflow-x:auto;white-space:pre;font-family:Consolas,'Cascadia Code',monospace;font-size:14px;line-height:1.55;"><code><span style="color:#F3F4F6;">bq mk --reservation --location=us-central1 --edition=ENTERPRISE_PLUS --slots=50 \
  --secondary_location=us-east4 lab-dr</span>
</code></pre>
</div>


2. **[SQL] Prepare a replicated dataset.**


<div style="margin:18px 0;border:1px solid #334155;border-radius:8px;overflow:hidden;">
<div style="background:#243244;color:#DBEAFE;padding:7px 12px;font-family:Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif;font-size:12px;font-weight:700;">
CODE • SQL
</div>
<pre style="margin:0;background:#111827;color:#F3F4F6;padding:16px;overflow-x:auto;white-space:pre;font-family:Consolas,'Cascadia Code',monospace;font-size:14px;line-height:1.55;"><code><span style="color:#F3F4F6;">CREATE SCHEMA lab23_dr OPTIONS (location = 'us-central1');
CREATE TABLE lab23_dr.orders AS
SELECT n AS order_id, CURRENT_TIMESTAMP() AS created_at FROM UNNEST(GENERATE_ARRAY(1, 1000)) AS n;
ALTER SCHEMA lab23_dr ADD REPLICA `us-east4` OPTIONS (location = 'us-east4');</span>
</code></pre>
</div>


3. **[SQL] Attach the dataset to the failover reservation.** Replace `YOUR_PROJECT`.


<div style="margin:18px 0;border:1px solid #334155;border-radius:8px;overflow:hidden;">
<div style="background:#243244;color:#DBEAFE;padding:7px 12px;font-family:Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif;font-size:12px;font-weight:700;">
CODE • SQL
</div>
<pre style="margin:0;background:#111827;color:#F3F4F6;padding:16px;overflow-x:auto;white-space:pre;font-family:Consolas,'Cascadia Code',monospace;font-size:14px;line-height:1.55;"><code><span style="color:#F3F4F6;">ALTER SCHEMA lab23_dr SET OPTIONS (failover_reservation = 'YOUR_PROJECT.lab-dr');</span>
</code></pre>
</div>


4. **[CLI] Assign the project.**


<div style="margin:18px 0;border:1px solid #334155;border-radius:8px;overflow:hidden;">
<div style="background:#243244;color:#DBEAFE;padding:7px 12px;font-family:Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif;font-size:12px;font-weight:700;">
CODE • BASH
</div>
<pre style="margin:0;background:#111827;color:#F3F4F6;padding:16px;overflow-x:auto;white-space:pre;font-family:Consolas,'Cascadia Code',monospace;font-size:14px;line-height:1.55;"><code><span style="color:#F3F4F6;">bq mk --reservation_assignment --reservation_id=$PROJECT_ID:us-central1.lab-dr \
  --job_type=QUERY --assignee_type=PROJECT --assignee_id=$PROJECT_ID
bq mk --reservation_assignment --reservation_id=$PROJECT_ID:us-central1.lab-dr \
  --job_type=PIPELINE --assignee_type=PROJECT --assignee_id=$PROJECT_ID</span>
</code></pre>
</div>


   Writes to datasets with disaster recovery must use Enterprise Plus slots, so load jobs need the `PIPELINE` assignment.

5. **[Console] Check the setup.** Open **Administration → Disaster recovery**. You see `lab-dr` with primary `us-central1`, secondary `us-east4`, and `lab23_dr` attached.

## Expected Result

| Thing | Reality |
|---|---|
| Edition | Enterprise Plus only |
| Failover reservation | Compute in two regions |
| Dataset | Replicated and attached |
| RTO | About 5 minutes after failover starts |
